## The problem
  Random errors in the logs in relation to the gogogate2 integration.
  Only stared happening once updated to 0.107.X versions


## Environment
<!--
Frontend version: 20200318.1 - latest
arch | armv7l
dev | false
docker | true
hassio | true
os_name | Linux
os_version | 4.19.93-v7l+
python_version | 3.7.6
timezone | Europe/Dublin
version | 0.107.3
virtualenv | false


-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue:  0.107.3 (any 107 version so far)
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 0.106.6
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Docker on raspbian
- Integration causing this issue: Gogogate2
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/gogogate2/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
-->

```
cover:
  - platform: gogogate2
    username: !secret gogogate_username
    password: !secret gogogate_password
    ip_address: !secret gogogate2_ip
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--

-->

```
 2020-03-21 13:45:36 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.helpers.entity] Update for cover.main_gate fails
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 279, in async_update_ha_state
    await self.async_device_update()
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity.py", line 476, in async_device_update
    await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(self.update)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/concurrent/futures/thread.py", line 57, in run
    result = self.fn(*self.args, **self.kwargs)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/gogogate2/cover.py", line 107, in update
    self._status = self.mygogogate2.get_status(self.device_id)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/pygogogate2/__init__.py", line 107, in get_status
    devices = self.get_devices()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/pygogogate2/__init__.py", line 80, in get_devices
    self.apicode = devices.find('apicode').text
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'find'
```

## Additional information
comments:
I has the same problem a while back and determined this issue was related to authentication credentials. https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/18887
TLDR; Wrong username/password or you are using a user other than admin to connect.
In my setup, connecting as admin works great once I was careful to copy/paste the passwords.

review_comments: Please rename to `device_state_attributes`.
Why are we checking if we should abort after creating the entry?
Why use the async api when the device library doesn't support that? It doesn't seem needed.

Consider using `DataUpdateCoordinator` directly since the only thing being added is the `api` object like the example here
https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/integration_fetching_data/#coordinated-single-api-poll-for-data-for-all-entities

`get_data_update_coordinator` is used in multiple places (__init__.py and in testing) to reduce duplicate code. I don't think I can create the update coordinator in __init__.py without introducing duplication.
Remove this.
Remove this.
This should be an unknown error.
Remove this.

```suggestion
        return self._data_update_coordinator.last_update_success
```
Never-mind, I see why you this below.
Don't access integration details in tests. Patch the library api instead.
Python 3.7 has dataclasses for this purpose.
Why do we need to process the core config?
I don't think we need this helper. Just inline the coordinator setup in `async_setup_entry`.
Why set up the cover domain?
We should not use integration details in tests.
Please rename to `test_config_flow.py` as its testing the config flow.

```py
domain_data = hass.data.setdefault(DOMAIN, {})
config_entry_data = domain_data.setdefault(config_entry.entry_id, {})
```
Please don't make helpers for assertion. That should be done in each test.
Use the core interfaces to start the tests. Here use `hass.config_entries.async_setup`.
We should not assert this exception but the state of the config entry. It will be `ENTRY_STATE_SETUP_RETRY`.
Don't call the coordinator in the tests. That's a detail that may change in the future. Patch time and fire a time changed event to take control over time and move it forward as needed.

See eg this test:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/65e509ed8f8791409072b9f1281cd70279367989/tests/components/gdacs/test_geo_location.py#L43
